A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same Ditto/Editto work. The main sections, equations, and retained results can be matched reliably. V1 includes appendices A–D; these are absent from the supplied v2, which ends after its references.

before.justification: V1 reports original Editto evaluations, a 1,000-rating human study, qualitative editing results, and ablations in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains the original quantitative evaluations, human-study scores, qualitative results, and training-data and curriculum ablations.

M1.justification: The synthesis pipeline, VACE-based architecture, reference-frame curriculum, flow-matching objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Explicitly naming Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen-Image identifies components already cited in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Ditto-1M, its global/local editing coverage, and synthetic-to-real experiments. V2 newly describes the existing evaluation as 50 non-Pexels videos with five instructions each; this does not establish changed coverage. Removed appendix examples illustrate already represented editing tasks.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain TokenFlow, InsV2V, InsViE, and qualitative Gen4-Aleph results. However, v1 Appendix B/Figure 9's comparison against VACE-Depth and VACE-Depth + Key Frame is absent from v2. Newly discussed Señorita and EditVerse are not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 omits Appendix B's controlled evaluation varying depth-only, original-keyframe, and edited-keyframe conditioning. The retained experiments keep their training budget, metrics, and human-evaluation criteria. The newly specified 50-video, five-instruction test setup is additional documentation, with no established revision to the existing evaluation.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix B's qualitative test of why the generator needs an edited keyframe alongside depth guidance disappears, as does the appendix prompt-distribution visualization. The main data-scale and curriculum ablations, synthetic-to-real demonstration, and trained-model versus generator analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The human-study total remains 1,000 ratings/votes; additional participant and test-set details do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1 contain identical scores, including Editto's CLIP-T 25.54, CLIP-F 99.03, and VLM 8.10. V2 removes the source-category counts and percentages in v1 Figure 3, generator-control outputs in Figure 9, and additional dataset/model examples and prompt visualization in Figures 11–12.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, including generator conditioning and the flow-matching loss, retain the same mathematical content. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: scalable high-quality synthesis, the million-example Ditto-1M dataset, modality curriculum learning, and state-of-the-art instruction-based editing. The expanded related-work discussion does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 omits Appendix B's interpretation that base VACE transfers motion effectively but has limited editing instruction-following, motivating edited-keyframe conditioning. It also newly characterizes the non-Pexels evaluation as out-of-distribution relative to training. The main interpretations of curriculum learning and scaling remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds the 50-video/five-instruction test-set description, identifies human judges as postgraduates and researchers, and explicitly states that pipeline components are open source. It omits Appendix C's randomized presentation and best-to-worst ranking procedure, and reduces hardware specificity from 64 NVIDIA H-series GPUs to 64 GPUs. The project-page link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds substantive contrasts with Señorita's task-specific expert system and EditVerse's use of in-context learning, alongside numerous additional background citations. V1's prior-dataset comparison table disappears. These extend the positioning while retaining the existing inversion-based/feed-forward framing.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order remain intact. Edits concentrate on the feed-forward related-work discussion, a shortened Section 4 title, terminology refinements, and replacing appendix cross-references with supplementary-material references. The appendix sections themselves are omitted.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the paper from one column to two, enlarges and repositions retained figures, and restyles the quantitative table. It removes v1's dataset-comparison table, source-category chart, and appendix Figures 9–12. The retained scientific illustrations largely show the same content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves evaluation transparency through test-set and participant details and updates related-work positioning. However, the supplied PDF loses the generator-conditioning analysis, human-study ranking documentation, and supplementary dataset/result evidence while retaining the same scores and claims. These omissions modestly weaken evidential support and reproducibility; the core method and main empirical findings remain intact.
